notes:
Account summary: Compilerly builds a code indexing and in-IDE copilot product aimed at mid-to-large engineering teams. Pushing to support both extremely low-latency streaming responses for in-editor completions (~10-40ms p99 target across localhost-like routing) and a separate high-throughput offline pipeline that refreshes embeddings for the entire customer corpus every 24-72 hours.

Key technical asks (from CTO / infra lead):
- Embedding refresh: ingest + vectorize ~500k files (avg 3k tokens/file) weekly; target 24-48h full refresh window for core repos, incremental updates within 2h.
- Indexing pipeline: parallelizable batch jobs, prefer server-side batching + prefix caching, replayable checkpoints for failed batches.
- In-IDE streaming: continuous token stream with per-keystroke hinting; need ultra-low tail latency and model pinning per customer (reproducible prompts).
- Model/version pinning: strict ability to pin LLM and quantization profile per release; rollback support for regressions.
- Cost control: aggressive batching & KV cache for embeddings to reduce token spend; interested in Optimize suggestions.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "We cannot have the model drift between release candidates — pinning + audit logs are non-negotiable." — CTO
- "If embedding refresh balloons cost, customers churn. Cost-per-update must be predictable." — Head of Product

Security / compliance notes:
- Must support SSO/SAML and enterprise KMS for key wraps. EU customers require data residency and audit trail for vector data retention. Legal asked for SOC2 + evidence of retention controls.

Procurement state / POC:
- Running a 3-week POC with Redwood Dedicated: scope = 1) embed-refresh throughput test (simulated 500k files), 2) in-IDE streaming latency test across regions, 3) model pin + rollback test.
- POC dataset + scripts uploaded to drive link above. 3rd week will be stress test with burst loads.
